# Sensitivity in sorting explained (2025-10-28 10:24Z)

_**User (2025-10-27 13:47Z)**_

What does sensitivity mean in sort?

---

_**Agent (model default, mode Agent)**_



---


`sensitivity` in `localeCompare` controls which differences affect comparison. In your code:

```29:29:app/static/chart_support.js
.sort((a, b) => a.localeCompare(b, undefined, { sensitivity: 'base' })); // Sort alphabetically (case-insensitive)
```

`sensitivity: 'base'` ignores case and accents, treating:
- `'a'` = `'A'` = `'á'` = `'Á'`
- `'e'` = `'E'` = `'é'` = `'É'`

**All sensitivity options:**
- `'base'`: ignores case and accents
- `'accent'`: ignores case; distinguishes accents (`'a'` = `'A'` but `'a'` ≠ `'á'`)
- `'case'`: ignores accents; distinguishes case (`'a'` ≠ `'A'` but `'a'` = `'á'`)
- `'variant'`: distinguishes all differences (case and accents; default)

Using `'base'` here ensures the sort is case-insensitive.

---

_**User (2025-10-27 13:47Z)**_

what is the default?

---

_**Agent (model default, mode Agent)**_



---

`sensitivity` defaults to `'variant'`, so it distinguishes case and accents.

Without specifying `sensitivity` in your code:

```javascript
.sort((a, b) => a.localeCompare(b));
```

This would treat `'A'`, `'a'`, `'Á'`, and `'á'` as different values. By setting `sensitivity: 'base'`, you make the sort case- and accent-insensitive.
